instruction:
Reconnected Supply Air System

Use the opened Bonsai IFC authoring environment to modify /home/user/Desktop/init.ifc by reconnecting the supply air system and exporting a connectivity summary. You may use /home/user/Desktop/init_plan.png as a local reference image. Save the outputs as /home/user/Desktop/result.ifc and /home/user/Desktop/result.csv. The IFC4 model must contain one project, one site, one building, and one storey named Ground Floor; three IfcDuctSegment entities; two IfcDuctFitting entities; two IfcAirTerminal entities; one IfcDistributionSystem; one IfcRelAssignsToGroup; thirteen IfcDistributionPort entities; and twelve IfcRelConnectsPorts relationships. Do not include spaces, walls, slabs, doors, windows, proxies, furniture, roofs, columns, beams, or stairs, and keep every IfcRoot GlobalId unique.

Name the distribution system Supply Air and assign exactly these products to it: Bend Fitting, Branch Segment, Main Segment 1, Main Segment 2, Terminal East, Terminal North, and Transition Fitting. Main Segment 1, Main Segment 2, and Branch Segment must be IfcDuctSegment entities; Bend Fitting and Transition Fitting must be IfcDuctFitting entities; Terminal East and Terminal North must be IfcAirTerminal entities. Assign all listed products to Ground Floor.

The CSV must use the exact headers GlobalId, Class, Name, SystemName, PortCount, ConnectedToCount and contain one row for each assigned product, matched by GlobalId. Report Bend Fitting as IfcDuctFitting with PortCount 2 and ConnectedToCount 4; Branch Segment as IfcDuctSegment with 2 and 4; Main Segment 1 as IfcDuctSegment with 2 and 2; Main Segment 2 as IfcDuctSegment with 2 and 4; Terminal East and Terminal North as IfcAirTerminal with 1 and 2 each; and Transition Fitting as IfcDuctFitting with 3 and 6. Every row must use SystemName Supply Air. Other representation details may vary.
